definitionEn: complete and not damaged, especially after something that could have caused harm
situation: Describing something that survived an accident, a disaster or a long period of time without being damaged.

examples.text: Although the storm destroyed half the village, the old church remained [[intact]].
Remarkably, she came through the scandal with her reputation [[intact]].
Thanks to the dry desert air, the ancient letters were found almost completely [[intact]].

texts: Somehow the glass vase arrived from Italy [[intact]].
The team kept its unbeaten record [[intact]] with a late goal.
Most of the town's medieval walls are still [[intact]].

badCollocation.noteRu: После intact не ставят from. Говорят survived the fire intact или untouched by the fire.

collocationTask.prompt: The old bridge ___ intact after the earthquake.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Remain intact — «остаться целым». Keep требует дополнения (keep something intact), а held и became здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: The seal on the bottle was still [[intact]], so we knew nobody had opened it.
nuance.explanationRu: Intact — о предметах, зданиях, репутации: целый, не повреждённый, не вскрытый. Unharmed — о людях и животных: невредимый.

reverse.text: The children were found cold but [[unharmed]] after a night in the forest.
reverse.explanationRu: О людях говорят unharmed или unhurt. Intact о человеке звучит так, будто речь о вещи.

fixIt.text: Luckily, the parcel arrived [[entire]]; not a single glass was broken.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Целый, неповреждённый» после глагола — intact. Entire значит «весь, целиком» и стоит перед существительным: the entire day.

reply.context: Your neighbour texts: "How's your house after the storm last night?"
options: Terrible! The whole roof is intact, so we'll have to replace it.
We were lucky. A few tiles are missing, but otherwise the roof is intact.
Please be advised that the property remains structurally intact at this time.
reply.explanationRu: Intact — «целый, без повреждений», поэтому второй ответ естественен. В первом intact противоречит ремонту, третий звучит как официальное уведомление, а не сообщение соседу.

rewrite.original: The vase wasn't damaged at all during the move.
rewrite.explanationRu: Survive something intact — «перенести что-то без повреждений».

definitionEn: the amount of food, drink or another substance that a person consumes
senseNote: Здесь — потребление еды и веществ; у слова есть и другие значения: набор студентов (the annual intake) и вдох (a sharp intake of breath).
situation: Talking about how much sugar, salt, alcohol or water a person consumes, usually in the context of health.

examples.text: Doctors advised him to reduce his salt [[intake]] to lower his blood pressure.
Athletes in training need to increase their daily [[intake]] of protein and water.
Cutting down on coffee after lunch reduced my caffeine [[intake]] and helped me sleep better.

texts: Try to keep your sugar [[intake]] below thirty grams a day.
The app tracks your water [[intake]] and reminds you to drink.
Pregnant women are advised to limit their [[intake]] of caffeine.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Приём пищи» — a meal: three meals a day. Intake — общее количество съеденного или выпитого: daily calorie intake.

collocationTask.prompt: Try to reduce your daily calorie ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Количество потребляемых калорий — calorie intake. Reception — «приём» гостей, income — доход, entry — вход или запись.

nuance.text: Cutting your sugar [[intake]] is one of the easiest ways to protect your teeth.
nuance.explanationRu: Intake — сколько еды или веществ поступает в организм. Admission — «приём» в другом смысле: вход, плата за вход, зачисление в вуз или больницу.

reverse.text: [[Admission]] to the museum is free on Sundays.
reverse.explanationRu: Вход в музей — admission. Intake — количество потребляемой еды или вещества.

fixIt.text: The nurse recorded the patient's fluid [[reception]] every two hours.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Приём жидкости» в медицинском смысле — fluid intake. Reception — приём гостей, стойка регистрации или качество сигнала.

reply.context: A friend says: "I get a headache every afternoon at work, and I don't know why."
options: You probably need a bigger intake of sleep, not more coffee.
Maybe check your water intake. I get headaches when I forget to drink.
One is advised to monitor one's fluid intake in accordance with medical guidance.
reply.explanationRu: Intake — о еде, напитках и веществах, поэтому второй ответ естественен. Сон не «потребляют» (intake of sleep), а третий ответ звучит как инструкция, а не совет другу.

rewrite.explanationRu: Reduce your sugar intake — «сократить потребление сахара».

definitionEn: being an essential part of something, so that the whole would be incomplete without it
senseNote: Не математическое «интегральный»: an integral part — неотъемлемая часть.
situation: Explaining that one element is so important to a system, team or tradition that it could not work without it.

examples.text: Customer feedback is an [[integral]] part of how we design new products.
Music and dance are [[integral]] to the festival, which celebrates the end of the harvest.
Trust is [[integral]] to any successful partnership, in business and in life.

texts: Public transport is an [[integral]] part of the city's climate plan.
Humour is an [[integral]] part of her teaching style.
Volunteers are an [[integral]] part of the hospital's daily life.

badCollocation.noteRu: Integral сочетается с to: integral to the project, или an integral part of the project.

collocationTask.prompt: Customer service is ___ to our success.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Integral to — «неотъемлемый для». Integrated — объединённый (integrated with, into), а entire и complete с to так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Good lighting is [[integral]] to the museum's design.
nuance.explanationRu: Integral — неотъемлемый, без него целого нет: integral to the design. Integrated — встроенный, объединённый с чем-то: integrated with the system.

reverse.text: The new app is fully [[integrated]] with our booking system.
reverse.explanationRu: Приложение, связанное с другой системой, — integrated with it. Integral with так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Tourism is an [[inalienable]] part of the island's economy.
fixIt.explanationRu: Inalienable говорят о правах: inalienable rights. «Неотъемлемая часть» чего-либо — an integral part.

rewrite.original: The festival would not be complete without music.
rewrite.explanationRu: Integral to или an integral part of — «неотъемлемая часть».

definitionEn: combining different parts or services so that they work together well as one system
situation: Describing a system, plan or service in which separate parts are joined so they work smoothly together.

examples.text: The city wants an [[integrated]] transport system where one ticket works on buses, trams and trains.
Patients benefit from an [[integrated]] approach in which doctors, nurses and social workers share information.
The new laptop has an [[integrated]] camera, so you don't need to plug one in.

texts: We need an [[integrated]] plan, not five separate projects.
Our office uses [[integrated]] software for payroll, holidays and expenses.
The hotel has an [[integrated]] system for booking rooms, spa treatments and tables.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Комплексный обед» — a set lunch или set menu. Integrated — о системах и подходах: an integrated approach.

collocationTask.prompt: We need a fully ___ approach to health and social care.
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Комплексный, единый подход» — an integrated approach. Complex значит «сложный», integral — «неотъемлемый», entire — «весь».

nuance.text: The school takes an [[integrated]] approach, linking science, art and history lessons.
nuance.explanationRu: «Комплексный подход» — an integrated approach. Complex значит «сложный, запутанный», и a complex approach звучит как «слишком сложный подход».

reverse.text: The instructions were so [[complex]] that nobody could put the desk together.
reverse.explanationRu: Запутанная инструкция — complex. Integrated описывает части, собранные в единую систему.

fixIt.text: By next year, every hospital in the region will use one [[united]] computer system.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Единая система» — an integrated или unified system. United — «объединённый» о людях и странах: the United Nations.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why did we switch to the new booking platform?"
options: Because it's integrated: none of its parts connect to anything else.
It was selected owing to its superior integrated synergistic functionality paradigm.
Because it's fully integrated with our calendar and payments, so nothing gets entered twice.
reply.explanationRu: Integrated — «связанный в единую систему», как в третьем ответе. В первом значение перевёрнуто, второй — набор модных слов вместо простого ответа коллеге.

definitionEn: the process by which newcomers become accepted, active members of a society or community
senseNote: Здесь — интеграция людей в общество; есть и техническое значение: integration of systems (объединение систем).
situation: Talking about how migrants, refugees or other newcomers learn the language, find work and become part of local life.

examples.text: Free language classes play a key role in the [[integration]] of refugees into local communities.
Sport can speed up the [[integration]] of newcomers, because it brings people together without much need for language.
The school runs a buddy scheme to help with the [[integration]] of students who arrive in the middle of the year.

texts: The city has a long history of successful [[integration]].
Learning the language is the first step towards [[integration]].
The report praises the town's approach to the [[integration]] of migrant families.

badCollocation.noteRu: Правильный предлог — into: integration into society. С to так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: После integration об обществе, группе или системе нужен into: integration into society. Onto, at и towards здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: Successful [[integration]] lets newcomers join local life while keeping their own language and traditions.
nuance.explanationRu: Integration — стать частью общества, сохранив свою культуру. Assimilation — полностью раствориться в большинстве, потеряв свой язык и традиции.

fixIt.text: Volunteers help with the social [[integrity]] of new arrivals in the town.
fixIt.explanationRu: Integrity — честность и порядочность. Процесс вхождения людей в общество — integration: social integration.

wordFormation.text: Shared community gardens have helped the [[integration]] of families from many different countries.

reply.context: At a dinner party, someone asks you: "How did you settle in when you moved to Canada?"
options: My integration was fast: I stayed at home and avoided everyone for a year.
Honestly, joining a hiking club did more for my integration than any official course.
My integration process was implemented in accordance with municipal protocols.
reply.explanationRu: Integration — вхождение в новое общество, и второй ответ описывает это естественно. Первый противоречит смыслу слова, третий звучит как отчёт чиновника.

definitionEn: the quality of being honest and keeping to strong moral principles, even when it is difficult
senseNote: Здесь — моральное качество; у слова есть и значение «целостность»: structural integrity.
situation: Praising someone who stays honest and refuses to break their principles, even when lying would be easier or more profitable.

examples.text: She has too much [[integrity]] to hide a mistake just to protect her bonus.
Voters want leaders with [[integrity]], not just good speeches and clever slogans.
The referee refused the bribe, and his [[integrity]] earned him respect across the league.

texts: He's a journalist of great [[integrity]] who always checks his sources.
Nobody questioned the judge's [[integrity]], even after the controversial ruling.
Say what you really think: [[integrity]] matters more than popularity.

badCollocation.noteRu: Integrity — неисчисляемое: с артиклем a и словом big не употребляется. Говорят great integrity или a person of integrity.

collocationTask.prompt: Accepting the gift would ___ her integrity.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчиво: compromise your integrity — «поступиться принципами». Break, spoil и lower с integrity не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The scientist showed real [[integrity]] when she published results that disproved her own theory.
nuance.explanationRu: Integrity — честность и верность принципам, даже себе во вред. Dignity — достоинство: умение держаться с самоуважением, например в поражении.

reverse.text: Despite losing the final, the team left the pitch with [[dignity]].
reverse.explanationRu: Держаться достойно после поражения — with dignity. Integrity — про честность и принципы, а не про манеру держаться.

fixIt.text: Everyone respects her [[principality]]: she never changes her views just to please the boss.
fixIt.explanationRu: Principality — княжество (например, Монако). «Принципиальность» — integrity: верность своим принципам.

reply.context: A friend messages: "My boss wants me to change the sales figures so they look better. What should I do?"
options: Don't do it. Your integrity is worth more than one good quarter.
Change them! That would show real integrity.
Pursuant to principles of integrity, falsification is contraindicated.
reply.explanationRu: Integrity — честность и верность принципам, и первый ответ это передаёт. Подделка цифр честности не показывает, а третий вариант звучит как юридическое заключение.

rewrite.original: Everyone knows he is honest and has strong principles.
rewrite.frame: Everyone knows he is a man of ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: A man (person) of integrity — «честный, принципиальный человек».

definitionEn: a well-educated person who spends time thinking and writing about serious ideas
senseNote: Здесь существительное (an intellectual — интеллектуал), а не прилагательное «умственный».
situation: Describing writers, thinkers and academics who take part in public debates about politics, culture or philosophy.

examples.text: He was a true [[intellectual]]: he read three newspapers a day and wrote essays on philosophy.
Some [[intellectuals]] look down on reality TV, but millions of viewers love it.
The shy student grew into one of the country's leading [[intellectuals]], famous for her essays on ethics.

texts: The magazine is popular with [[intellectuals]] and university students.
In the 1960s, many [[intellectuals]] left the country in search of freedom.
The novel mocks [[intellectuals]] who talk about ideas but never act on them.

badCollocation.noteRu: Про способного к математике говорят good at maths или brilliant at maths. An intellectual — человек, увлечённый идеями, философией, культурой.

collocationTask.prompt: She is one of the country's leading public ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Public intellectual — известный мыслитель, который выступает в публичных дебатах. Intellects и brains — «умы» в другом смысле, а public geniuses так не говорят.

nuance.text: He never went to university, but he became a respected [[intellectual]] through reading and writing.
nuance.explanationRu: Academic — преподаватель или исследователь в вузе, это профессия. Intellectual — человек, живущий идеями, диплом для этого не нужен.

reverse.text: She is an [[academic]] who teaches medieval history at a large university.
reverse.explanationRu: Должность в университете — academic. Intellectual — не профессия, а тип человека.

fixIt.text: My grandfather was a real [[intelligent]]: he read Tolstoy and argued about philosophy.
fixIt.explanationRu: Intelligent — только прилагательное «умный». «Интеллигент, интеллектуал» — an intellectual.

wordFormation.text: The mayor invited a group of [[intellectuals]] to discuss the future of the city.

reply.context: A friend asks about your new flatmate: "So, what's he like?"
options: He may be classified as an intellectual according to standard sociological criteria.
A total intellectual: he never reads and hates talking about ideas.
A bit of an intellectual. He reads philosophy at breakfast and wants to debate everything.
reply.explanationRu: An intellectual — человек, увлечённый идеями, как в третьем ответе. Во втором описан его противоположный тип, а первый звучит как научный отчёт, а не разговор с другом.

definitionEn: to become greater, stronger or more serious, or to make something do this
situation: Describing a storm, conflict, competition or effort that grows stronger, or someone making it stronger on purpose.

examples.text: Residents were told to leave because the storm is expected to [[intensify]] overnight.
Competition between the two supermarket chains has [[intensified]] since the new store opened.
Police have [[intensified]] their search for the missing hiker, adding helicopters and fifty more volunteers.

texts: The heat [[intensified]] as the afternoon went on.
Pressure on the manager [[intensified]] after a fifth defeat in a row.
The debate [[intensified]] when the minister refused to answer questions.

badCollocation.noteRu: Громкость не intensify, а turn up the volume. Intensify — о шторме, конкуренции, усилиях, давлении.

collocationTask.prompt: The police have ___ their efforts to find the stolen painting.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Усилить старания — intensify (или step up) your efforts. Enforce — следить за соблюдением закона, thicken и enlarge — о толщине и размере.

nuance.text: The rain [[intensified]] during the night, and several roads flooded.
nuance.explanationRu: Intensify — стать сильнее и острее: дождь, жара, конкуренция, давление. Strengthen — сделать крепче или прочнее: мышцы, отношения, позиции.

reverse.text: Swimming will [[strengthen]] the muscles in your back.
reverse.explanationRu: Укрепить мышцы — strengthen. Intensify — усилиться по интенсивности (дождь, спор), а не стать крепче.

fixIt.text: The conflict between the two neighbours [[aggravated]] after the new fence went up.
fixIt.explanationRu: Aggravate — переходный глагол: aggravate a problem. Сказать, что конфликт сам «обострился», — the conflict intensified.

wordFormation.text: Scientists warn that heatwaves will [[intensify]] as the climate warms.

definitionEn: the strength, force or seriousness of something, such as heat, light, feelings or effort
situation: Describing how strong a feeling, a light, a storm or a period of exercise is.

examples.text: Runners can measure the [[intensity]] of their training by checking their heart rate.
The [[intensity]] of her reaction surprised everyone; she was usually so calm.
The [[intensity]] of the light decreases as you move further away from the lamp.

texts: Nobody expected the storm to hit with such [[intensity]].
The actor plays the role with remarkable [[intensity]].
Cycling at low [[intensity]] is a good way to recover after a race.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Интенсивность движения» — traffic volume или просто heavy traffic. Intensity — о силе чувств, света, жары, нагрузки.

collocationTask.prompt: Interval training at high ___ burns a lot of calories.
collocationTask.explanationRu: At high intensity — «с высокой интенсивностью». Intense и intensive — прилагательные, а strength говорят о силе мышц или прочности материалов.

nuance.text: The [[intensity]] of the midday sun makes it dangerous to walk without a hat.
nuance.explanationRu: Intensity — сила или мощность чего-то: солнца, звука, чувства. Tension — напряжение, натянутость в отношениях или обстановке.

reverse.text: [[Tension]] between the two departments has been growing for months.
reverse.explanationRu: Натянутые отношения — tension. Intensity между людьми так не описывают.

fixIt.text: In July the [[tension]] of the heat makes it hard to work outside after noon.
fixIt.explanationRu: Сила жары, света или звука — intensity. Tension — напряжённость в отношениях или натяжение каната.

wordFormation.text: The [[intensity]] of the music made the final scene unforgettable.

rewrite.original: The storm was much stronger than anyone had expected.
rewrite.frame: The ____ of the storm surprised everyone.

definitionEn: involving a lot of concentrated work, effort or attention within a limited time
senseNote: Кроме базового intensive course (B1), важны intensive talks, intensive care (реанимация) и labour-intensive (трудоёмкий).
situation: Describing work, training, talks or treatment that packs a lot of effort into a short period.

examples.text: After three days of [[intensive]] talks, the two sides finally reached an agreement.
Before the exam, she did a week of [[intensive]] revision, studying from morning till night.
Premature babies often need [[intensive]] care for several weeks after birth.

texts: The police launched an [[intensive]] search for the missing boy.
Ten days of [[intensive]] rehearsals left the whole cast exhausted.
She is slowly recovering after a course of [[intensive]] treatment.

badCollocation.noteRu: Яркий цвет или сильный запах — intense, а не intensive. Intensive — о работе и усилиях: intensive training, intensive talks.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ farming uses large amounts of fertiliser and machinery.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Intensive farming — интенсивное сельское хозяйство с удобрениями и техникой. Intense, intentional и extended с farming так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Picking grapes by hand is labour-[[intensive]], so wine from small farms costs more.
nuance.explanationRu: В сложных словах labour-intensive, energy-intensive («трудоёмкий», «энергоёмкий») нужен intensive. Intense — «сильный, острый» о чувствах, боли, цвете.

reverse.text: The pain was so [[intense]] that she couldn't sleep.
reverse.explanationRu: Сильная боль, жара или эмоции — intense. Intensive говорят о работе, обучении и лечении.

fixIt.text: After the operation, she was moved to the [[intense]] care unit for two days.
fixIt.explanationRu: Реанимация — intensive care unit. Intense значит «сильный, острый» (intense pain) и в этом сочетании не используется.

wordFormation.text: All hotel staff receive [[intensive]] training in first aid.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How's the new job going?"
options: Exhausting! The first month is intensive training, eight hours a day.
Great, it's really intensive: I only work two hours a week.
My employment is currently characterised by intensive onboarding protocols.
reply.explanationRu: Intensive — «напряжённый, с большой нагрузкой», как в первом ответе. Два часа в неделю — не intensive, а третий ответ звучит как пресс-релиз, а не разговор с другом.
